blocks.text: HAVANA, Cuba — Cuba’s “reparto” genre has soared from humble beginnings to center stage of the Latin American music scene, counting Spanish superstar Rosalia and Puerto Rican artist Daddy Yankee among its fans. Emerging roughly two decades ago in so-called “repartos,” working-class neighborhoods on the outskirts of Havana, the genre did the rounds on cell phones and USB sticks before blowing up on social media. A slick blend of energetic rhythms, catchy hooks and a generous dose of slang about money, parties and sex, reparto draws inspiration from Cuba’s timba style and Latin America’s world-famous reggaeton.
